clue.text: An opportunity for revolutionary to seize South African political party

indicators.note: to seize something is to grab hold of it, so one piece closes around the other

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
the African National Congress

explanation.surface: A rebel sees an opening to take over a South African party.
explanation.definitionFit: A chance is an occasion when something becomes possible, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Correspond with head of college about criminal record

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of the word
on as in a talk on a subject
form is British slang for a criminal record

explanation.surface: Someone writes to a college principal about their criminal past.
explanation.walkthrough: Having form, in British slang, means having previous convictions.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform to something is to match or agree with it, as corresponding does.

clue.text: In reserve team after Adrian's debut

indicators.note: after tells us the word before it is placed second, behind the next piece
a debut is a first appearance, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: first letter of the name
a sports side is a team

explanation.surface: A player named Adrian makes his first appearance in the reserve team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In reserve team' reads as the reserves, but 'In reserve' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Money put aside is kept back for later, which is what holding it in reserve means.

clue.text: Jazz fan collects American books on advanced musical composition

indicators.note: collecting things gathers them in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
A is the abbreviation for American
the New Testament books of the Bible
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A jazz lover gathers American books on advanced composition.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the last piece after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a vocal composition with instrumental accompaniment, typically in several movements.

clue.text: Penny lied about getting round daughter to go

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for penny

indicators.note: getting round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps around another
moved about means jumbled, so the letters of the word next to it get rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone told a fib about taking their daughter somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters wrap around D after P leads. To piddle is informal British slang for urinating, so 'to go' is the euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Needing to go is a polite way of saying needing the toilet, and piddling is urinating.

clue.text: Encourage awareness in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so the word is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: insight is perceptive awareness

explanation.surface: A plea to promote awareness through talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to urge or stir someone on, usually to action, so a stronger form of encouraging.

clue.text: Frank's at a disadvantage — just

parts.note: being down means behind or losing
just and right both mean fair

explanation.surface: A man called Frank is losing out, and only just.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a name, but it is the adjective meaning blunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright describes plain, blunt speech or manner, the sense of frank as outspoken and direct.

clue.text: Organs fitted with adaptor essentially as a protective device

indicators.note: fitted with something means having it put in, so a letter is slotted inside

parts.note: ear and lug, two words for the organ of hearing; lug is informal

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so the central letter of the word is taken

parts.note: central letter of the seven

explanation.surface: Body parts kitted out with an adapter make up some protective gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Organs is plural because two different words for the ear are wanted; lug is informal British for an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: An earplug is a small device placed in the ear to protect it from noise or water.

clue.text: Firmness of purpose shown by Will

definitions.meaning: second meaning: willpower, the drive to carry something through

explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Will makes it look like a man's name; it is the noun for resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Determination is the quality of sticking to a decision, which is both resolve and strength of will.

clue.text: Opposed to a character like Hamlet? Not half

indicators.note: not half tells us to drop half of the word, keeping only the other half

parts.note: Hamlet is a flawed, brooding protagonist, a classic antihero

explanation.surface: Someone disapproves of a figure like Hamlet, or only half does.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the eight letters, the second four (HERO) go, leaving ANTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti is a preposition meaning against, standing opposed to some idea or person.

clue.text: Famous player's role can do with being revised

indicators.note: a revised text is rewritten and reworked, so the letters before it are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A well-known actor's part could do with a rewrite.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward was an English playwright who also acted on stage and screen, so a celebrated player.

clue.text: Vogue article featuring northern Italian city

parts.note: a vogue is a fashion, a mode
N is the abbreviation for northern
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fashion magazine piece focuses on a city in northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Modena is a city in the Emilia-Romagna region of Italy, home of balsamic vinegar and Ferrari.

clue.text: Dishonest bishop leaves Irish city altogether

indicators.note: when someone leaves they are no longer there, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: bent is slang for crooked
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
IR is the abbreviation for Irish
Ely, the cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A corrupt bishop departs from a city in Ireland for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish city' reads as one place in Ireland, but it splits into two pieces, the city being Ely in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirely and altogether are both adverbs meaning completely, wholly, in every respect.

clue.text: What little kids have as weapons

definitions.meaning: first meaning: children's limbs are small
second meaning: firearms carried by hand, like pistols and rifles

explanation.walkthrough: The playful first reading takes the phrase literally; the second is the military term for handheld guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Small arms is the standard term for portable firearms such as rifles, pistols and light machine guns.

clue.text: Initially looked into borrowing before accepting money for rake

indicators.note: initially points to the starts of words, so the first letter of each is taken

parts.note: first letters of the three words

indicators.note: accepting something takes it in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone first investigated taking out a loan before agreeing to cash for a garden rake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' suggests the garden tool, but it is the old word for a dissolute man.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a man given to immoral, pleasure-seeking living, exactly what a libertine is.

clue.text: Excited by Gone Girl's opening

parts.note: in the past, as in years gone or years ago

indicators.note: an opening is the very start of something, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by the start of the thriller Gone Girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog describes someone eagerly excited and impatient to hear or see more.

clue.text: Dress designer finally gets an award

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word, so only its last letter is taken

parts.note: last letter of the word
Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: A fashion designer is at last honoured with an award.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour given by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To robe someone is to dress them, especially in ceremonial clothing, so both work as verbs.

clue.text: Withdraw pamphlet in support of Religious Education

parts.note: the school subject abbreviation
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious

explanation.surface: A religious leaflet produced to back up RE lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, a piece in support of another sits beneath it, so RE goes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to take it back, to withdraw it formally.

clue.text: Found in an FE college perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to set up or establish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past tense of find, but it is the verb to establish. FE is further education, British post-school study below degree level.
explanation.definitionFit: To institute something is to establish it, and an institute is a body set up for education or research.

clue.text: Wrong to retain workers from Harrow

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so one piece keeps the other within it

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
workers as men

explanation.surface: A misguided bid to keep staff from Harrow, the famous school.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow looks like the London school; it is the verb meaning to distress.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrow is to cause someone acute distress, which is what tormenting them does.

clue.text: Right about needing a small amount of paste

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: RT is an abbreviation for right
an ounce is a tiny quantity

explanation.surface: Someone using only a dab of paste, wallpaper or otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paste' suggests glue, but it is the slang verb to beat soundly.
explanation.definitionFit: To paste an opponent is informal for thrashing them, and trounce means to defeat heavily.

clue.text: Practice needed after Bangladesh's opener gets an edge

indicators.note: an opener is the first in, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of the name
an order is an established procedure or practice

explanation.surface: A Bangladeshi opening batsman gets an edge after net practice.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket: an opener is a first batter, and an edge is a ball off the side of the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A border is the edge or margin of something, such as a page, garden or country.

clue.text: Begin to set up in the open air

parts.note: to start a business is to set it up
outdoors, out

explanation.surface: Someone getting ready to pitch a stall outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting out is the phrasal verb for commencing, setting off on a course or career.

clue.text: About to eject Republican from crime debate

parts.note: re means concerning, about

indicators.note: ejecting someone throws them out, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: the crime of setting fires
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Someone is planning to throw a Republican out of a debate on crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crime debate' reads as one phrase; 'crime' is wordplay and 'debate' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason with someone, or reason something out, is to argue it through logically, a verb sense of debate.

clue.text: A friend of a friend in Paris meets with success

parts.note: the French word for a friend
as in making a go of something

explanation.surface: A French friend's friend does well.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for friend, widely used informally in English too.

clue.text: Bob for example finds prime land to develop around Ohio

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the letters close about the next piece
developing land reshapes it, so these letters are built into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder
O is the US state abbreviation

explanation.surface: A man called Bob finds a good plot of land to build on near Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob looks like a person's name, but it is offered as a word that reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A palindrome reads identically in both directions, and the name Bob is one such example.

clue.text: Contributing to erosion around island

indicators.note: letters that contribute to a phrase form a part of it, so the solution sits inside the words

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Something adding to the wearing away of the coast round an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, famous for its abbey.

clue.text: Right to ring ambassador for an explanation

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: the political right, Conservatives
His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: The right decision is to phone the ambassador to get an explanation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests a phone call but means surround. A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed account of why something happens, an explanation yet to be proven.

clue.text: An inspired act of resistance to contain City? Just the opposite

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so one piece goes within another
this flips the instruction just given, so the holder and the held swap roles

parts.note: Stoke-on-Trent, the English city, or its football club Stoke City
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A brave act of defiance holding back City's attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' reverses the instruction, so the city holds the resistance rather than the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroke of genius or inspiration is a single brilliant act, so stroke alone means one.
